expect:
Award up to 8 marks using a best-fit approach:
Top band (7-8): Thorough discussion of both VFX and SFX with analysis and a justified conclusion.
Upper-mid band (5-6): Good discussion with analysis of both sides.
Lower-mid band (3-4): Some discussion with limited analysis.
Lower band (1-2): Basic points with little development.
Indicative content:
VFX advantages:
• Can create effects impossible to achieve physically (e.g. dragons, space)
• Safer — no risk of injury from pyrotechnics
• Can be edited and refined after filming
• Can be more cost-effective for large-scale effects
VFX disadvantages:
• Requires expensive software and skilled artists
• Can look unrealistic if poorly done
• Time-consuming post-production process
SFX advantages:
• Look more realistic and tangible on screen
• Actors can react to physical effects naturally
Conclusion: Most modern films use a combination of both.

expect:
Award up to 8 marks using a best-fit approach:
Top band (7-8): Thorough discussion with analysis of benefits and potential drawbacks of extensive pre-production.
Upper-mid band (5-6): Good discussion with analysis.
Lower-mid band (3-4): Some discussion with limited analysis.
Lower band (1-2): Basic points.
Indicative content:
Importance of pre-production:
• Planning saves time and money during production
• Storyboards/scripts ensure the team has a clear vision
• Research identifies target audience needs
• Risk assessments ensure health and safety
• Work plans keep the project on schedule
• Client briefs are agreed before production starts
Counterpoints:
• Spending too long on pre-production can delay the project
• Plans may need to change during production anyway
• Over-planning can stifle creativity
Conclusion: Pre-production is essential for professional, well-organised media products.

expect:

Upper-mid band (5-6): Good discussion with analysis.
Lower-mid band (3-4): Some discussion with limited analysis.
Lower band (1-2): Basic points.
Indicative content:
Permanent staff:
• Already know the company’s brand and values
• Available immediately, no recruitment delay
• Consistent quality and communication
• More expensive long-term (salaries, benefits)
Freelancers:
• Specialist skills for specific tasks (e.g. hiring a VFX specialist)
• Only paid for the project — can be more cost-effective
• Fresh perspective and new ideas
• Less control over quality and availability
• May not understand the brand as well
Conclusion: A combination is often best — permanent staff for core work, freelancers for specialist tasks.
